I should:

- HEAD@{1}: commit: Move to Stanford (this is 650dba4)
- HEAD@{2}: checkout: moving from master to HEAD~1 (this is interesting - it seems like someone did a checkout from master to HEAD~1, which would put you in detached HEAD state)
- HEAD@{3}: reset: moving to d7d3e4b (this reset master back to d7d3e4b)
- HEAD@{0}: checkout: moving from 650dba4 to master (this is when the user checked out master, leaving 650dba4 dangling)

So the sequence was:
1. User was on master at d7d3e4b
2. User checked out HEAD~1 (putting them in detached HEAD state at c4e38a1)
3. User made a commit "Move to Stanford" at 650dba4
4. User reset master back to d7d3e4b (losing the reference to 650dba4)
5. User checked out master, leaving 650dba4 dangling

The solution is to merge or cherry-pick commit 650dba4 into master. Let me do that.
